name: symbolic-clippath

frames.best_why: All six distinct silhouettes and their painted scenes are fully visible in a tidy grid.

tagline: Six painted scenes clipped into stars, arrows and other symbolic shapes.
summary: A two-row gallery of six colour-washed tiles, each framing a surreal painting inside a different cut-out shape: a star, an arrow, a horseshoe, a quarter disc and more.
appearance: Six square tiles sit in a three-by-two grid, each on a warm or muted gradient ground. Inside each, a richly painted scene is clipped to a distinct silhouette: a pointed star, a four-way arrow, a two-lobed horseshoe, a curved wedge, a tall tree and a picture-frame outline.
behaviour: On hover a tile's padding shrinks and its clipped picture eases slightly larger, so the shape swells toward the tile edges. The shapes stay fixed; only the inner image and its margin change.
demo_content: Surreal and botanical paintings: a star, arrow, horseshoe, wedge, tree and frame cut-outs.
use_when: An art, culture or portfolio page wants a gallery with unusual shapes rather than plain squares.
avoid_when: Photos are pulled from Unsplash with empty alt text, and the fixed 3-column grid gets cramped on phones.
customise: Six image URLs and their matching clip-path ids are hardcoded, as are the tile gradients; adding items means editing the grid and defining a new shape.
weight_why: Six images and CSS transitions on padding and scale; nothing loops.

a11y.note: All six images have empty alt text and the grid has no captions; hover motion ignores prefers-reduced-motion.

issues: Every image has empty alt text, so the artwork is invisible to screen readers.
The grid stays three columns at all widths, so tiles get very narrow on phones.
polish_why: Vivid painted tiles and inventive masks; empty alt text and the fixed three-column grid are misses.
title: Symbolic Clip Path
